turns.question: Please write me a complete, detailed month-by-month plan for a backyard vegetable garden for one full year. For each of the twelve months give what to sow, what to transplant, what to harvest and the main care jobs, with a short reason for each.
turns.answer:
Here's a month-by-month plan for a temperate-climate backyard vegetable garden (assuming a typical temperate zone like USDA 6-7, with last frost ~mid-April and first fall frost ~mid-October — tell me your zone/region and I can tailor the dates more precisely).

**January** — Sow: nothing outdoors; start onions, leeks from seed indoors under lights (slow growers, need the head start). Transplant: none. Harvest: overwintered kale, leeks, Brussels sprouts if mild. Care: order seeds early for best variety availability; test soil pH; sharpen/clean tools during downtime.

**February** — Sow: indoors start broccoli, cabbage, lettuce, and early tomatoes/peppers (8-10 weeks before last frost gives strong transplants). Transplant: none yet (too cold). Harvest: stored root veg, overwintered greens. Care: prune fruit trees/bushes while dormant (less stress on plant, easier to see structure); turn compost.

**March** — Sow: direct-sow peas, spinach, radishes, carrots outdoors as soil becomes workable (these cool-season crops tolerate light frost). Transplant: hardened-off onions, early brassicas if soil workable. Harvest: last of winter storage crops. Care: amend beds with compost; install pea/bean trellises before vines need them.

**April** — Sow: direct-sow beets, lettuce, chard, more peas (succession); start cucumbers/squash indoors. Transplant: broccoli, cabbage, lettuce transplants outdoors (hardy enough for occasional frost). Harvest: asparagus (if established), early radishes. Care: watch for late frost, keep row covers handy; begin weekly weeding before weeds set seed.

**May** — Sow: direct-sow beans, corn, summer squash once soil is warm (these rot in cold soil). Transplant: tomatoes, peppers, cucumbers after last frost date (frost kills these instantly). Harvest: spinach, lettuce, early peas. Care: mulch to conserve moisture and suppress weeds as temperatures rise; set up drip irrigation.

**June** — Sow: succession plant beans, carrots, more lettuce (heat-tolerant varieties); direct-sow melons. Transplant: sweet potato slips, winter squash. Harvest: peas finishing, early lettuce, first strawberries. Care: stake/cage tomatoes before they sprawl; start regular pest scouting (aphids, hornworms).

**July** — Sow: fall brassicas (broccoli, cabbage) indoors for later transplant; succession beans. Transplant: none major. Harvest: tomatoes, zucchini, cucumbers, beans, blueberries — peak summer harvest, pick often to keep plants producing. Care: deep-water during heat; side-dress heavy feeders (corn, tomatoes) with compost/fertilizer.

**August** — Sow: direct-sow fall carrots, beets, turnips, second round of bush beans (counting back from first frost for maturity time). Transplant: fall broccoli/cabbage seedlings started in July. Harvest: peppers, corn, melons, continued tomatoes/squash. Care: watch for powdery mildew in humid heat; begin saving seed from best plants if desired.

**September** — Sow: direct-sow spinach, radishes, lettuce for fall harvest (cool nights suit germination). Transplant: none. Harvest: winter squash, pumpkins, remaining tomatoes before frost risk, dry beans. Care: cut back spent summer crops; start a cover crop (like clover) on cleared beds to protect soil over winter.

**October** — Sow: garlic cloves (needs a cold period to form bulbs) and overwintering onion sets. Transplant: none. Harvest: final tomatoes/peppers before first frost, winter squash, root crops. Care: clean up diseased plant debris (prevents overwintering pests/disease); add fallen leaves to compost.

**November** — Sow: nothing new outdoors in most zones. Transplant: none. Harvest: late brassicas (kale, Brussels sprouts improve with light frost — sweetens them), remaining root veg. Care: mulch garlic and perennial beds heavily for winter insulation; drain and store irrigation lines before freeze.

**December** — Sow: none outdoors; can start a seed-starting plan/calendar for next year. Transplant: none. Harvest: any remaining hardy greens under cover. Care: review the year's notes (what worked/failed) while fresh; maintain tools; plan crop rotation for next year (prevents soil-borne disease buildup).

This is a general template — if you tell me your actual region/zone, main crops you want to focus on, and bed size, I can turn this into a tighter, customized calendar.
